question: When talking to patients, what is the main goal of guidance compared to counselling?
explanation: Think of guidance like pointing someone in the right direction with practical information. You've got this! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h1)

question: Why do we bother with guidance and counselling in nursing?

options.A: They replace the need for physical medical treatments
options.B: They empower patients to take charge of their health
options.C: They eliminate all psychological stress for patients
options.D: They guarantee complete compliance with hospital rules

explanation: Great nursing isn't just about pills and injections; helping patients understand their choices gives them power over their own wellness! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h1)

question: Where would you most likely give general health guidance to a group of people?
explanation: Guidance is often broad and preventive. A busy clinic waiting room is a classic spot to share health tips with groups! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h2)

question: How does counselling differ from simple guidance?

options.B: Counselling focuses strictly on career choices
options.C: Counselling only deals with physical symptoms
options.D: Counselling focuses on internal feelings and behaviors

explanation: While guidance gives direction, counselling digs a bit deeper into a person's emotions and psychological state. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h2)

question: As student nurses, we always hear about confidentiality. What does it actually mean?

options.A: Documenting all personal feelings in public charts
options.B: Keeping patient information private and secure
options.C: Sharing patient stories with the entire clinic staff
options.D: Telling family members everything the patient says

explanation: Confidentiality means what happens in the counselling session stays between you and the patient. Trust is everything! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h3)

question: Is there ever a time when a nurse can break patient confidentiality?

options.A: When the nurse wants to gossip with friends
options.B: When a coworker is simply curious about the diagnosis
options.C: When the patient misses three clinic appointments
options.D: When there is a risk of severe self-harm or abuse

explanation: Patient safety always comes first. If someone is in danger of hurting themselves or others, keeping them safe overrides privacy rules. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h3)

question: A patient needs help managing their diet, exercise, and chronic illness. What type of counselling is best?
explanation: When the focus is on daily habits like eating well and staying active to manage a condition, it's health and lifestyle counselling! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h4)

question: A patient is feeling completely overwhelmed after just finding out they have diabetes. Which counselling approach fits best?
explanation: Dealing with the emotional shock and lifestyle changes of a new diagnosis falls right under personal-social and emotional support. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h4)

question: What is the very first thing you must do when starting a counselling session with a patient?
explanation: Before any healing conversation can happen, the patient needs to feel safe and welcome with you. Rapport is key! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h5)

question: Why do nurses do an evaluation stage at the end of a counselling process?

options.A: To collect payment for the session
options.B: To review the progress made toward set goals
options.C: To extend the therapy sessions indefinitely
options.D: To punish the patient for not following advice

explanation: Evaluating lets you and your patient look back and celebrate how far they've come toward their goals! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h5)

question: Why are open-ended questions so helpful during a patient chat?

options.A: They encourage patients to share more details
options.B: They prevent the patient from crying
options.C: They shorten the length of the clinical visit
options.D: They force the patient to answer with a simple yes

explanation: Questions starting with 'How' or 'What' invite patients to open up and tell their story in their own words. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h6)

question: Which action shows that a nurse is truly practicing active listening?

options.A: Giving full attention and minimizing distractions
options.B: Interrupting to offer quick medical solutions
options.C: Looking around the room for the next client
options.D: Writing in a chart while the patient speaks

explanation: Active listening means putting other tasks aside and showing the patient they have your complete, caring focus. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h6)

question: If a primary health care nurse sends a patient to see a mental health specialist, what is this action called?
explanation: When a patient needs specialized care beyond general nursing, connecting them to an expert is called making a referral. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h7)

question: Why are primary health care nurses usually the ones doing community counselling?

options.A: They are often the first point of contact for community members
options.B: They have legal authority to prescribe psychiatric drugs
options.C: They have specialized degrees in clinical psychology
options.D: They spend most of their time in large urban hospitals

explanation: Because primary care nurses work right in the community, people naturally trust them and turn to them first for help. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical barrier to effective nursing counselling?

options.B: Having too much uninterrupted personal time
options.D: Severe time constraints in busy clinics

explanation: In real-world clinics, we almost always wish we had *more* time, never too much of it! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h8)

question: How can nurse burnout negatively affect counselling sessions?

options.B: It reduces the nurse's ability to show empathy
options.C: It removes all language barriers in the room
options.D: It improves the speed of patient discharges

explanation: When you're exhausted and burnt out, it's so much harder to find the emotional energy to deeply connect with your patients. Take care of yourselves, future nurses! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h8)
